title: Senior's toolkit: scikit-learn as teams use it
summary: Splits, pipelines, column transformers, cross-validation, grid search, reports and notebook hygiene.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: scikit-learn as teams use it
steps.body: You built models by hand to see inside them. At work the same steps are scikit-learn calls, and the habit that matters most is putting every preprocessing step inside a `Pipeline`, so nothing from the test data leaks into training.

toolkit.what: Hold back data the model never sees while you build it.
flags: keep the class balance the same in both parts
toolkit.example: X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2, stratify=y, random_state=42)

toolkit.what: Chain preprocessing and the model into one object. `fit` learns scaling only from the training data, and the same steps run at prediction time.
Different preprocessing per column type: scale the numbers, one-hot encode the categories.
flags: a name, a transformer, the columns
a category unseen in training becomes all zeros instead of an error
what to do with other columns (the default drops them)

toolkit.what: Score a pipeline on several train/validation splits of the training data: a far steadier estimate than one split.
toolkit.example:
scores = cross_val_score(pipe, X_train, y_train, cv=5, scoring="roc_auc")
print(scores.mean(), scores.std())

toolkit.what: Try settings with cross-validation and keep the best. Inside a pipeline, name a parameter as `step__param`.
flags: the step name, two underscores, the parameter

toolkit.what: Precision, recall and F1 per class on the test set, in one table. Accuracy alone hides a model that ignores the rare class.
Save the fitted pipeline (preprocessing and model together) to load in a service or a batch job.
flags: load; use the same scikit-learn version

toolkit.what: In Jupyter (Kernel menu) or VS Code (Restart, then Run All): prove the notebook works top to bottom with no hidden state before you share a number from it.
flags: reload your own modules after you edit them

steps.prompt: A churn model scores 0.99 ROC-AUC in cross-validation and 0.62 in production. The notebook runs `StandardScaler().fit_transform(X)` on all rows, then splits, and one feature is `days_since_cancellation`. What is the problem?
options: Leakage: the scaler saw the test rows, and `days_since_cancellation` is only known after a customer has churned. Drop the future column and put the scaler inside a Pipeline
Production data is always worse; 0.62 is expected
ROC-AUC is the wrong metric; use accuracy
steps.explain: Scores that look too good usually are. A feature that encodes the answer is target leakage and is the bigger problem here; fitting preprocessing outside the pipeline leaks too. A pipeline only fixes the second, so ask "would I know this at prediction time?" for every column.

steps.prompt: The nightly scoring job crashes with `ValueError: Found unknown categories ['Wales'] in column 0 during transform`. Training data had no customers from Wales. What is the standard fix?
options: `OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore")` in the pipeline, then retrain and redeploy
Delete customers from Wales before scoring
Retrain every night including the scoring data
Convert the region to a number with `astype(int)`
steps.explain: New categories appear in real data all the time. `handle_unknown="ignore"` encodes them as all zeros; also log how often it happens so you know when to retrain.

steps.prompt: Put a leak-free modelling workflow in order.
lines: X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, stratify=y, random_state=42)
also: X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, stratify=y, random_state=42)
steps.explain: Split first, so the test rows never influence anything. Cross-validate on the training set to compare choices (it fits fresh copies, so it does not matter whether it comes before or after the final fit), and score on the test set once, at the end.

steps.prompt: Split keeping the class balance, then cross-validate with ROC-AUC.
code: X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2, __1__=y, random_state=42)
steps.explain: `stratify=y` keeps the share of each class equal in train and test, which matters when the positive class is rare. `scoring` picks the metric.

steps.prompt: Match each argument to its meaning.
pairs: same class balance in train and test
a parameter of one pipeline step

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Put every preprocessing step inside a `Pipeline`, compare models with `cross_val_score` on the training set, and touch the test set once at the end. Before you report a score, restart the kernel and run all cells, and ask of each feature: would I know this at prediction time?
